J-05.name: Aggregates are precomputed at ingest, never on the fly
J-05.note: REGRESSED passing->failing. RAW browser-qa UT-J-05 FAIL (.llm.md): the backfill+storage-serving assertions held (2010-07-15 backfill completed ok, drawdown_expectations warmed), but the step-4 acceptance ('while a heavy ingest job runs, poll GET /api/health; assert it stays responsive throughout') FAILED hard -- GET /api/health connection-timeout (curl exit 28/000) for 7+ continuous minutes during a SECOND back-to-back heavy ingest; backend hit its own enforced memory_cap_mb=6144 ulimit -v ceiling with a worker-thread MemoryError; /proc showed the process alive but fully idle (all 22 threads futex_do_wait) -- a hang, not slow compute; required a manual restart to recover. Screenshot J-05-backend-hung-checking.png corroborates (frozen 'Checking backend...' skeleton). iter-6 had explicitly verified 'health 200 on 20/20 polls during the job', so this is a genuine passing->failing move on the literal acceptance. Attribution to iter-7's diff is contested (earlier unrelated /api/backtest MemoryErrors predate the test -> pre-existing capacity fragility on the grown live DB), but the new synchronous per-claim drawdown_expectations warm runs on the ingest finalize hot path and browser-qa declined to wave it away as unrelated. NOT adjudicable as a false positive (unlike iter-5's stale golden proxy): literal acceptance step, live-observed, modified code path.

J-06.name: Pages load only what they need
J-06.note: Stays partial. The TARGET fix is genuinely delivered & verified: UT-02 real-browser first /evidence view after a real ingest measured 22.4ms (was ~73s cold-miss), drawdown_expectations warmed, byte-identical values (UT-06); audit re-traced identical warm/read cache keying. BUT J-06 is NOT a clean pass: overall browser-qa verdict = FAIL, and browser-qa found a live /api/backtest -> forward_aggregates_cached -> large ScannerResult MemoryError on an on-load path (directly contrary to J-06's 'no on-load endpoint memory-exhaustion' audit clause), plus the 7-min hang produced a frozen frame rather than the honest progress state J-06's Acceptance requires. Perf-budgets' 11-page reconfirmation is curl-warm (method disclosed), not a clean real-browser 11-page sweep. Do NOT redo the drawdown warm itself -- the residual is the availability/capacity failure it surfaced (see J-05).

anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: AG-3: A journey passes ONLY if the displayed numbers are correct — they match the engine's computation for the same as-of date — not merely that the page renders.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: Interrupted backfill rows served a fabricated '0 calendar days · 0 already snapshotted · 0 non-trading' breakdown for ranges that were really hundreds of days (browser-qa UT-14, reproduced twice on 517-day jobs). FIXED intra-iteration by the audit (B1): _run_detail gates the four breakdown fields to null on _breakdown_computed (calendar_days>0). Confirmed in working tree: apps/backend/app/engine/data_manager.py:3017,3032-3035.

anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: AG-8 — Resilience to data-shape and data-scale change: widening the data basis (deeper history) must never crash an existing page or exhaust a service's memory; the UI degrades gracefully (contained error boundary, honest '—'/NA placeholder, never a blank/frozen frame); unbounded whole-table ORM loads forbidden on the deep basis.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: browser-qa UT-J-05 (raw .llm.md) + reports/qa/goal-ops-hardening-iter-7-evidence/J-05-backend-hung-checking.png + logs/backend.log MemoryError signature: during a heavy ingest on the grown live dev DB the backend exhausted its enforced memory_cap_mb=6144 ulimit -v ceiling (worker-thread MemoryError, no traceback -- too exhausted to format one), GET /api/health hung 7+ minutes (all 22 threads futex_do_wait), the UI showed an ambiguous frozen 'Checking backend...' rather than the honest 'Backend unavailable' state, and recovery required a MANUAL restart -- the exact failure mode AG-8 forbids. A separate live /api/backtest -> forward_aggregates_cached -> large ScannerResult MemoryError on an on-load path was also observed. ATTRIBUTION CONTESTED: earlier unrelated /api/backtest MemoryErrors predate the test (pre-existing capacity fragility) so this may not be caused solely by iter-7's diff, but the new synchronous per-claim drawdown_expectations warm runs on the ingest finalize hot path and browser-qa declined to attribute it away.
